_doc: Board qualification is derived: every protection type in the graph (including LSID) must compile without refusals and be in this build's units_at_parity, the silent DT/tuning wiring self-check must pass for this board, blob hash and kernel release, and the verified extraction record must bind the tuning to this Mac's own macOS. Missing, failed or stale records keep the speakers muted on v2 kernels. denied_boards and board_overrides (allow/deny) are policy only: deny wins, and allow never bypasses compilation, parity, provenance or self-check. Provisioning and self-check may run before qualification; only a current qualified record admits the supervisor. LSID is at parity only where the compiler releases it: a companion whose estimator is never run, beside a complete LSM2 model (the four-lane J713/J813 tunings), runs on that static model. A companion the compiler still mutes (lsm2-release-gated, e.g. the six-lane K114/K116) fails provisioning, so those boards stay muted.
_voicing_pre_doc: Full generated voicing deployment overrides per physical board: literal true enables it, false keeps the interim convolver. At runtime a board without an override automatically compiles its own full chain; offline fixture artifacts retain their recorded mode. SPP3V owns promotion after numerical/acoustic qualification. Provision again after any change.
_voicing_pre_bound_doc: Keyed by the speaker identity the tuning bundle names (its AID), not the board (2026-11-21): AID13 (the J413's speakers) woofers -0.043 / tweeters 0. The 0 dB entries (AID9, AID35, AID44) had no effect and are dropped; the values are unchanged. What it is: an interim never-louder bound, one gain in dB (<= 0) per unit lane, applied by the PipeWire voicing graph after the voicing plugin, so that no lane of the generated voicing is louder than macOS while a voicing law is still open. It is derived from our full-chain safety scan of v2's voicing against the macOS chain's own render (bound.py: worst louder excess + 0.03 dB, L/R pairs equal); protection is unchanged and governs. Each entry goes when its speaker's laws are exact. History: 2026-11-07 first bounds on four boards while the Comp onset/param-69 and the AID44 q2 detector laws were open (J413 woofers -1.09 dB). 2026-11-08: J413 woofers -0.883/-0.884 dB and J316s -0.097 dB came from references that were not the macOS chain; against corrected references (each Mac's DSP-database strip for its speaker ID, and the property strip) the J413 woofers need -0.041 dB (woofer bursts at velocity 1.0013x, VirtBass/Tone onset precision) and every other lane 0; re-run on the next tree: J413 woofers -0.043 dB, all else 0. A 0 means that lane is at parity on every scan row.
_voicing_pre_lowpass_doc: Keyed by the bundle's speaker identity (AID<n>), like voicing_pre_bound_db (2026-11-21). Interim never-louder band limit, not a macOS law. {hz, order}: an even-order Butterworth low-pass built from PipeWire bq_lowpass sections in FRONT of the voicing plugin. History: 2026-11-07, J700 only: v2's AID44 ControlFreak lacked the AU's reconstruction low-pass, so above ~17 kHz the box was up to +23 dB (+30 dB at 0 dBFS) louder than macOS and its saturation aliased a loud high-frequency input into 9-16.5 kHz; the lane trim could hold neither. 17.4 kHz order 8 (with the J700 trim): AID44 box rig (installed AU, 362 tones/pink/steps incl. 16-23.75 kHz probes) 0 louder cases, worst -0.58 dB; full AID44 voicing VLS 30 Hz-19.5 kHz 0 louder bands, worst -0.03 dB; cost at 16 kHz -0.1 dB. 2026-11-08: the AID44 ControlFreak saturation, reconstruction and drive laws are exact on the box rig (steady and 20 kHz), so no speaker carries the low-pass; the mechanism stays for a future open law.
_operating_volume_cap_doc: Per board: a cap on the operating volume, dB on the amp volume control's own TLV, from -40 to 0. It only lowers what the machine reports and is never a value of its own: the operating volume is the ceiling the card reports under the grant (every amp volume's TLV maximum: 0 dB, or on a machine whose speaker only a lease may lift, macaudio spk_fixed_ceiling, that ceiling: the J873g's -16 dB, aurora-silicon/linux#1862). The self-check records the cap (selfcheck.bind volume_cap_cdb); the supervisor grants only while every amp sits exactly at the card's ceiling and that ceiling is at or below the cap. A card that reports no ceiling is never granted, with or without an entry here. No board needs one today; anything malformed refuses the board.
_playback_rows_doc: Protected playback rows on record, by the tuning bundle's speaker identity (AID<n>, as identify names it). A row is sound played through speakerguardd v2's protection on that speaker and measured with V/I sense and the Mac's own microphone. covers: 'loud-step' = a step to full volume (slider 1.0); 'thermal-ramp' = a sustained hold long enough for the thermal model to climb (minutes), with the protection's temperatures and gain recorded. A speaker is proven when its rows (each with evidence) cover playback_covers; a silent self-check pass is not a playback row. Two users: provisioning refuses a graph with a protection type in units_need_playback_rows on a speaker that is not proven (LSID's static release, which runs the four-lane J713/J813 tunings open loop on their LSM2 model, so unproven speakers like AID42 stay muted until rows exist), and aurora-speaker-upgrade's boot unit switches no unproven speaker to v2 (by hand, `run` still can). A speaker with no rows (AID42) is not proven. Add a row only with its evidence.
